data.name: NoAnswerFromTool
data.value: No answer from {0}: {1}
data.comment: {0} is the MCP tool name and is never translated. {1} is what was recorded with the failure, written by whatever refused and English whatever the reader's language, so it is quoted rather than translated. One key for all five model-management tools: the broker records the exception type name as the failure code, so a refusal by rule and a fault arrive under the same one, and a word that told them apart would be a guess.

data.comment: No full stop after the command in either language: a trailing period gets copied into a shell.

data.name: ProfileHasItsOwnPipeline
data.value: Task profile '{0}' has a pipeline of its own: a model chosen for the log, the log read in fragments, the findings merged. Neither ask_local nor localai ask runs any of it. Send the log to triage_log, or to localai triage on the command line.
data.comment: The guard both surfaces cross, and the only one ask_local has: the console refuses in AskCommand.TryParse before any broker work, and nothing refuses an MCP caller earlier than this. Separate from NotATextChatProfile, which stays for the seven profiles that really are not text-chat ones -- a refusal naming a cause that is false is the mistake AskProfileNotSupported's own comment records. Both routes are named because this string cannot know which surface is asking, and an agent has both. Profile and tool names are identifiers and stay Latin in both languages.

data.name: TooManyFiles
data.value: {0} files exceed the {1}-file limit for one call; split the request.

data.name: TooManyImages
data.value: {0} images exceed the {1}-image limit; split the request.
data.comment: The limit is over the request, checked at the metadata pass before a byte is read. It no longer says "for one call": in the default form the images are not one call - each is read on its own and the readings are merged.

data.name: TranslateFileEmpty
data.value: The file '{0}' is empty, so there is nothing to translate.
data.comment: Whitespace only is empty here too, because that is what the task's own ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace would reject a moment later with a vaguer sentence. One sentence for both faces: the console's --in and translate_local's path.

data.name: TranslateFileMissing
data.value: There is no file at '{0}'.
data.comment: {0} is the resolved absolute path, never the path as typed: a relative path run from the wrong directory is the commonest cause, and only the resolved form shows it. Shares file_missing with TranslateNotAFile.

data.name: TranslateFileNotRead
data.value: The file '{0}' could not be read: {1}
data.comment: {1} is the framework's own message, English under the --json pin and the machine's language otherwise. The console maps this to exit 66, EX_NOINPUT, the mirror of the 73 --out gives when it cannot write.

data.name: TranslateFileNotText
data.value: '{0}' is not text: it contains a zero byte, which no text file has.
data.comment: The sentence names the check the code performs: a zero byte in the first 8000 bytes, skipped when a UTF-16 or UTF-32 BOM says the file decodes. Any looser wording would be a claim about content this does not inspect.

data.name: TranslateMarkdownOn
data.value: '{0}' is Markdown, so markdown was on: fenced code passed through untranslated. Pass markdown false to translate it as plain text.
data.comment: Past tense, and inside the answer rather than before the run: an MCP caller cannot stop a run the way a person watching a console can, so the line reports what was assumed instead of warning. CliText.TranslateMarkdownAssumed is the console's present-tense twin.

data.name: TranslateNeedsOutPath
data.value: '{0}' is {1} characters, past the {2}-character limit for a translation returned as text. Give outPath and the document is written to disk instead.
data.comment: Refused before the model runs. The limit is on what may land in a caller's context, not on what may be translated, which is why outPath lifts it. {1} and {2} are invariant.

data.name: TranslateNotAFile
data.value: '{0}' is a directory, not a file to translate.
data.comment: Shares file_missing with TranslateFileMissing because the remedy is the same, and keeps its own sentence because the reader who typed one made a different mistake - the pair TriageEmptyInput and TriageNoSource already work this way.

data.name: TranslateNotWritten
data.value: The translation could not be written to '{0}': {1}. It was not kept — fix the path and call again.
data.comment: The sentence has to say the translation is gone: handing back a document the caller asked to be written to disk would drop everything outPath saved into its context as a surprise. CliText.OutputNotWritten stays separate because it does not carry that fact.

data.name: TranslateOutputDirectoryMissing
data.value: There is no directory for outPath '{0}'. Nothing was translated yet; create it and call again.
data.comment: Checked before the run rather than after it: a missing directory discovered at the end of twenty minutes of GPU work is the one failure with nothing left to recover.

data.name: TranslateOutputIsDirectory
data.value: outPath '{0}' is a directory. Name the file to write.
data.comment: outPath stays Latin in every language: it is a parameter name, as ExactlyOneSource already spells path and text.

data.name: TranslateOutputIsSource
data.value: {0} and {1} name the same file '{2}'. Give the translation a name of its own.
data.comment: Translating in place destroys the original and there is no undo. {0} and {1} are the two names of the face that refuses - the console passes --in and --out, translate_local passes path and outPath - so one sentence serves both. The paths are compared resolved, so {2} is the resolved form of both.

data.name: TranslateReplaced
data.value: An existing file at that path was replaced.
data.comment: Visibility instead of prohibition: refusing to overwrite would fight the main use, and the workaround it invites - delete the target first - is worse when a run dies halfway. Joined to TranslateWritten by a single space.

data.name: TranslateSourceAmbiguous
data.value: Give exactly one of source or path: source is text already in hand, path is a file this reads itself.
data.comment: Not ExactlyOneSource, which names path and text: translate_local has no text parameter, and naming a parameter the tool does not have sends the caller to fix the wrong thing.

data.name: TranslateSourceMissing
data.value: Nothing to translate: give the text as source, or a file as path.
data.comment: The pair of TranslateSourceAmbiguous, and the reason both name the parameters rather than the concepts: the caller is a model choosing arguments.

data.name: TranslateWritten
data.value: Translation written to '{0}' ({1} KB, {2} characters). The document is on disk, not in this answer.
data.comment: {1} and {2} are invariant. The sentence says where the document went because the answer deliberately does not carry it.

data.name: ImagesReadOneAtATime
data.value: Images read one at a time and merged: {0} — {1}
data.comment: The counted form's detail. Separate from ImagesRead because the two are different claims about the answer: one look at five images can compare them and five merged readings cannot, which is what the merge prompt forbids. A reader deciding whether to trust a statement spanning the images has only this line to go on. Renders inside Notice's hole, so no trailing full stop.
